intro.en: Ironmongery items, accessible ironmongery and ironmongery for specific uses, keyed to the Door and Ironmongery Schedule.

text.en: Ironmongery shall be supplied to the Door and Ironmongery Schedule, which lists each door mark against a hardware set (HS codes) and each item by hardware code. All items shall come from [[mfr]] so that finishes and fixings match. Submit the full schedule with product data, and fire test evidence for items on fire-rated door sets, to {{CA}} for approval at least [[weeks]] weeks before ordering. The keying system shall be approved before any lock is ordered, and every item shall be labelled with its door mark on delivery.

mfr.default: one manufacturer or one coordinated supplier

options.v: one manufacturer or one coordinated supplier
options.en: one manufacturer or one coordinated supplier

options.v: the named manufacturer listed in the schedule
options.en: the named manufacturer listed in the schedule

guidance.en: A set-based schedule keeps the specification short and makes changes easy to track door by door. Mixing suppliers commonly leads to mismatched finishes and items outside the fire door evidence.

text.en: Ironmongery shall be [[finish]] unless the schedule states otherwise. Items shall meet corrosion resistance grade [[corr]] to BS EN 1670. Fixings shall be of a compatible metal and finish to avoid bimetallic corrosion.

options.v: powder coated or PVD finish as scheduled
options.en: powder coated or PVD finish as scheduled

guidance.en: Grade 304 stainless steel is commonly used for interiors; grade 316 is usual for external doors, coastal sites and pool areas, where 304 tends to tea stain in Hong Kong's salty air.

text.en: Hinges shall be [[htype]] to BS EN 1935, grade [[hgrade]], with [[qty]] hinges per leaf, or as required by the fire door evidence. Hinges on fire-rated door sets shall be the type covered by that evidence.

hint.en: from the classification code, e.g. grade 13

guidance.en: Heavy solid core and fire doors on busy corridors commonly take a higher grade hinge, and a fourth hinge on tall leaves helps resist warping. Hinge grade and size should match the leaf weight and the closer.

text.en: Door closers shall be [[ctype]] to BS EN 1154, power size [[power]] to suit the leaf width and weight. Closers shall have [[feature]]. Closers on fire-rated door sets shall be covered by the fire door evidence.

guidance.en: Closers set too strong are a common complaint and can make doors hard to open for wheelchair users and children. Floor springs are typical on glass entrance doors and heavy double-swing doors; check the screed depth for the floor box early.

text.en: Escape doors shown on the schedule shall have [[exit]]. Devices shall be compatible with the door, frame and any fire rating, and shall be operable from the escape side without a key. Locations shall be as required by the project's fire safety strategy and comply with the Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings 2011 (2024 Edition).

options.v: panic exit devices with horizontal bar to BS EN 1125
options.en: panic exit devices with horizontal bar to BS EN 1125

options.v: emergency exit devices with lever or push pad to BS EN 179
options.en: emergency exit devices with lever or push pad to BS EN 179

options.v: panic or emergency exit devices as scheduled door by door
options.en: panic or emergency exit devices as scheduled door by door

guidance.en: Panic bars (BS EN 1125) are typical where members of the public may use the exit and are not familiar with it; lever or push pad devices (BS EN 179) are commonly used where occupants are staff trained in the escape route. Check which applies with the fire engineer before ordering.

text.en: Locks and latches shall be mortice type to BS EN 12209, backset [[backset]] mm, with functions as the schedule; WC indicator bolts shall be releasable from outside in an emergency. Locks and latches on fire-rated door sets shall be covered by the fire door evidence. Cylinders shall be [[cyl]], keyed to a key plan with [[levels]] agreed with {{CA}} and the Employer before cylinders are ordered. Use construction keys or cores during the works and change to the permanent keying at handover.

hint.en: e.g. grand master, floor master, individual

options.v: restricted key section with registered keys
options.en: restricted key section with registered keys

options.v: compatible with an electronic access control system
options.en: compatible with an electronic access control system

guidance.en: The key plan is commonly left until late, which delays cylinder orders and handover; a restricted key section stops copies being cut at a local key shop. Check the leaf stile width before fixing the backset, as a short backset pinches knuckles on narrow-stile doors.

text.en: Pairs of doors with rebated meeting stiles that close on their own shall have a door coordinator to BS EN 1158, so the leaves always close in the right order. The inactive leaf shall be held by [[bolts]]. On fire-rated pairs, the coordinator and bolts shall be covered by the fire door evidence, and bolts shall not stop the inactive leaf closing in a fire unless the fire door evidence allows it.

options.en: automatic flush bolts top and bottom
lever action flush bolts top and bottom
the closer and coordinator only, with no bolts

guidance.en: Without a coordinator, a rebated pair often closes out of order and the active leaf stays ajar, which defeats a fire door. Manual flush bolts left engaged are a frequent finding on fire door inspections, so automatic bolts are common on escape routes.

text.en: Lever handles shall comply with BS EN 1906, category of use [[cat]], on [[rose]]. Levers shall be a returned design that does not catch clothing. Levers on fire-rated door sets shall be covered by the fire door evidence.

guidance.en: Category 4 is commonly chosen for public buildings and heavy-use doors, category 3 for offices and homes. Returned levers are typical on escape routes and accessible doors.

title.en: Door stops and fire door signs

text.en: Provide [[stop]] to every door that could strike a wall, fitting or another door. Fire-rated doors shall carry the fire door notices of {{ref:SGN-FIR-010}}, in a finish to match the ironmongery.

options.v: overhead stops integrated with the closer
options.en: overhead stops integrated with the closer

guidance.en: Floor stops are a trip hazard on escape routes and under raised floors, so wall or overhead stops are often preferred there. Bilingual fire door signs are typical in Hong Kong.

text.en: Where the schedule shows a fire door held open, provide [[hold]] to BS EN 1155, linked to the fire alarm system so that the door releases and closes on alarm or loss of power. The interface with the fire alarm shall be coordinated with the fire services installation and shall be as required by the project's fire safety strategy.

options.v: separate wall or floor electromagnetic holder
options.en: separate wall or floor electromagnetic holder

guidance.en: Hold-open devices stop fire doors being wedged open on busy corridors, a frequent finding at fire inspections. Commonly the wiring and alarm interface are missed between the joinery and fire services packages, so name who supplies and connects them.

text.en: Ironmongery on accessible routes shall comply with the Design Manual: Universal Accessibility 2026 (formerly the Design Manual: Barrier Free Access 2008). Lever handles shall be mounted at [[height]] mm above finished floor level and contrast visually with the door. The opening force at the leading edge shall not exceed [[force]] N for internal doors and [[forcefd]] N for external doors and fire doors on accessible routes. Closers on internal doors shall take at least 3 seconds to move the door from 70 degrees open to 75 mm from closed.

guidance.en: Opening force is where accessible doors most often fail in use, usually because closers are left at factory setting. Coordinating handle height with vision panels and push plates avoids clashes on the door face.

text.en: Fix ironmongery to the manufacturer's templates and recommendations, using all fixing holes and the screws supplied. Prepare leaves and frames for ironmongery in the factory where possible. Do not cut intumescent material or the leaf core beyond what the fire door evidence allows. Remove ironmongery before decoration or protect it fully, then refit and adjust.

guidance.en: Site cutting for locks and closers is a common way fire door sets lose their rating. Factory machining to the approved schedule is typical practice for fire-rated doors.

text.en: At completion, adjust every closer for closing speed, latching and opening force, and check that all locks and exit devices work freely. Hand over [[keys]], a keying schedule cross-referenced to door numbers, special tools, spare parts and an operation and maintenance (O&M) manual with product data and servicing intervals. Readjust closers [[readjust]].

hint.en: e.g. 3 keys per cylinder and 2 master keys

options.v: before the end of the defects liability period
options.en: before the end of the defects liability period

options.v: once after six months of occupation
options.en: once after six months of occupation

readjust.default: before the end of the defects liability period

guidance.en: Closers settle and doors drop in the first months of use, so a return visit to readjust is commonly included. Keys handed over loose without a schedule cause problems for facilities managers for years.

text.en: Electric locks on exit routes shall release on power failure and on fire alarm. Exit doors shall open from inside without a key. [[extra]]

options.en: Encased push bars shall not be used.

guidance.en: Licence conditions for hotels, guesthouses and care homes.

text.en: Every food room and toilet door shall have a closer. Doors shall have stainless steel push and kick plates, and exit doors shall have keyless exit hardware.

Accessible guestrooms, at not less than 2 per 100 rooms or part thereof with a minimum of 2, shall have visual doorbells and room numbers in Braille and raised characters mounted between 900 mm and 1,500 mm above floor level.

guidance.en: The ratio follows the hotel licensing conditions and the access manual; the visual doorbell is best practice.

title.en: Closers on staircase and lobby doors

text.en: Closers on doors to required staircases and their protected lobbies shall not allow a check action to hold the door open, and these doors shall have no hold-open device. Notices reminding users to keep the doors closed shall be fixed to both sides as {{ref:SGN-FIR-010}}.

guidance.en: FS Code 2011 (2024 Edition) Clauses B13.7 and C16.2, checked 9 Nov 2026.
